generations.prompt: Late afternoon, low golden sun and long shadows, dust hanging in the light. A high, wide view of a large modern archaeological excavation in a field at the edge of a forest: a rectangular trench the size of half a field, cut in stepped levels about a meter and a half deep, with straight walls and baulks of dark earth, string lines on pegs, aluminium ladders, wheelbarrows and buckets, a sieve station, and a white canopy with a table at the rim. The trench floor is dark wet earth with black water pooling in the lowest parts; in the deepest corner a square sondage holds a pool of black oily mud with a dull sheen. Eight people in muted field clothes and blue nitrile gloves work spread out through the trench, some standing shoulder-deep against the walls with mattocks and trowels, two carrying buckets up a ladder, one at the sieve. The camera drifts forward very slowly and smoothly over the site. Modern equipment only. No music, no speech. No on-screen text, no captions, no watermark.
